slice.leaf: Inspect exact rmcp-v3.1.4 ServerHandler tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel seams plus stock TaskManager/TaskContext ownership to test application-owned durable task-store decoupling while tool creation stays router-first.
slice.finding: At the released ServerHandler boundary, tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel are ordinary overridable handler methods taking only protocol params plus RequestContext<RoleServer>; the generic dispatcher capability-checks and then calls self.get_task/self.update_task/self.cancel_task. Their signatures do not require TaskManager or TaskContext, and the defaults are method_not_found. Therefore an application can keep router-first tools/call while implementing these three protocol methods against its own durable task store without coupling those handlers to stock TaskManager. However stock TaskContext is not backend-pluggable: it owns private task_id plus Arc<Mutex<TaskManagerInner>>, TaskManagerInner is private, and TaskManager::spawn constructs that context internally after allocating a fresh UUID task in its own in-memory map. The released public API therefore does not let an application reuse stock TaskContext/request_input/cancellation against an application-owned durable store.
slice.architecture_boundary: Protocol-method decoupling is positive; stock execution-context reuse is blocked. A custom persistent create-or-get path can override task query/update/cancel, but restart-safe execution, input routing and cooperative cancellation require an application-owned executor/context (or an SDK change), not merely a custom store behind stock TaskContext.
scope_limits: No claim that a full durable executor is implemented or compile-tested in this runtime.

No claim that custom task creation is yet proven independent of TaskManager; the next slice must pin CallToolResponse::Task/CreateTaskResult construction and registered-tool return conversion at the same exact release.
Resident execution/redrive and external-effect idempotency/fencing remain separate unresolved proof obligations.

acceptance_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_or_user_e: UNRESOLVED_OVERALL_ROUTE: an application-owned resident executor/context is still required for restart-safe execution and in-task input/cancellation; no accepted Chat-native replacement has been proven.
